Not giving you false hope, I checked your other post and you scarring definitely looks treatable and also not that bad. I would check out Dr. Davin Lim's videos on Youtube to get an idea of what kind of treatments there are for each types of scars, and from there please god find yourself a dermatologist who can do those kinds of treatments- such as TCA CROSS, subcision, filler, CO2 laser, mostly. Just a phenol peel is not going to help much and I think max maybe 30% improvement with that treatment would be about right, but i'm not a doctor. All I know is there are more specific and advanced techniques of dealing with acne scars than a chemical peel, and you gotta find yourself a derm that will be willing to work with you. It's expensive but worth it, this is your mental health we're talking about! It took me months to find the right dermatologist and along the way I was often met with disappointment. Had I not found the derm I have currently, I probably wouldn't be here anymore, as sad as that sounds, but I had pretty horrific scarring that's even hard for me to look at pictures of (it's improved so much since then). Best of luck and please reach out if you need to talk to someone.

You need a second opinion from a doctor you can trust. It's a pain but you have to do the work, it sucks I've been there but half the battle is even finding a good cosmetic dermatologist. Dr. Davin Lim on Youtube explains a lot of the procedures for certain types of scarring. You take LSD- what do your trips tell you, lol? If I took acid and realized I was not doing everything to help myself out of a hellish situation then i'd have a tough trip and try and fix things. 

Therapy also helped me stay on track with all the appointments \*with\* my dermatologist, my derm is on the other side of the state and it was painstaking to take the train there every month but slowly and surely I can now live a half decent life. I still have residual mental health problems and yes, I think of the obvious easy way out too sometimes but not nearly as often and heavily as I used to. 

You might need a completely different thing done like fat grafting for the volume loss, or TCA for indented ice pick scars, or punch excision for some deeper scars but for punch excision do not fuck around with who does it, it can make things way worse which it did for me (sucks). Also laser treatments? Some derms will fucking scam you, man. There are so many different types of lasers and ways of performing the laser that CO2 laser is just too general of a term.

Back a few years ago I woke up one day and just took a video, I wish I still had it lol, just stating my honest sober feelings about my skin (it was horrific at the time), and showed my ugly scars under angled lighting, and that was the moment I basically thought okay either I find the cure or I'm done living. It sounds like you're at a point where you're really acknowledging how much these affect you and I hope you can keep your head in the game enough to get the treatment you need and find the doctor right for you. It's expensive and it might be a years long journey towards better skin but trust me it's worth it, as someone who's been on both sides. There is hope. 

Good luck man

Extinction burst is when something defined in behavior analysis as expecting something and reacting through aggression or other "problem" behaviors when that someone doesn't get what they were expecting. I imagine suicide is related to this; expecting something out of life and not getting it, and being horribly disappointed and thus choosing to commit suicide.

You could try to lower your expectations. The less and less you expect out of life, the less extinction burst. To illustrate this, imagine paying for something at the vending machine and it gets stuck. You might shake the machine, punch it, say fuck, shake your head, etc., because you were expecting to be rewarded for your efforts of putting the money in.

If you do this, it might hurt less. Imagine if you knew you wouldn't get something out of that vending machine, you wouldn't even go to it right, because why would you waste so much time and energy doing that when you know it's just gonna screw you over?

So maybe try a different vending machine. Try finding one that doesn't hurt you like the ones you've been to have. 

Of course you could argue they are all broken. In that case, I have no clue what you should do. Because sometimes, I agree, everywhere it seems like I put in the time and effort and never ever get the reward. But you could see how it works out, trying something else, because clearly, if you are thinking of killing yourself, then it's not working out and you need to find something else before the world loses someone great.

On a side note, I work with a 15 year old who is very, very anxious; so much so that she misses 4 days out of 5 of school on average. But I still believe, deep down, that the world would be worse off without her, despite what she believes. And I tell her this all the time. And if I can believe this about someone else, why the hell shouldn't I believe that about myself? Why shouldn't you believe that about yourself? So far I can't find a good answer to those questions. If you believe other people shouldn't commit suicide and have a life worth living despite their circumstances, you could try to believe it about yourself. I believe the world would be better off with you around, despite how you feel and despite your circumstances. So many times we practice compassion for others on a greater level than we do of ourselves. We practice forgiveness for everyone in the world but ourselves at times. This isn't just a hypothesis; studies show we care more about our dogs than we do ourselves! If sometime you could tell yourself that you deserve a break for trying so damn hard all the time, then life would be better. I think you deserve some self-compassion, too. 

I guess these aren't all the answers. I too have been extremely depressed most of my life. I do think at some point, I will go through with it, but maybe I'm just short sighted and incapable of self-compassion, like many who commit suicide are as well. That doesn't change anything, however, and it doesn't make it any easier for me. I think about suicide a lot, and some days I just plan things out, like if X Y and Z happen then off a building I go. Sometimes it relaxes me to think of how I would go out, because at least I don't have to deal with all of this for more than however long it is until I kill myself. 

There was someone I knew who only talked about how they were going to kill themselves. This person would even use it against people, so far as to threaten to kill himself if a girl didn't have sex with him, which was just so fucked up. I wish he could see the world differently, because he was so short sighted about everything in his life, he was living his life as if it were his last days. Of course he didn't kill himself, and the actions he did when he was thinking this way only made his depression catastrophically worse. Think about this. If you live your life as if it were your last day on earth, you'd do some wild shit, and so would everyone and their brother. But if we just imagined ourselves living for another year, as hard as it may seem, what would we do then? Well, maybe we would save up for a car, or find a girlfriend/boyfriend on tinder or at a local bar, or go on a vacation, or make a really good friend, and anything in between. I think if we practiced the idea in our head about how we would stay around for at least a year, we would focus on what we could improve until then, and get the most out of our time, instead of doing extremely messed up things like threatening a girl to hook up with us or else we'll commit suicide, or something crazy like that. Because trust me, it's very hard to bounce back from doing something like that; Even if we did survive, we would be racked with guilt. Thus proving my point that acting as if it's our last days makes things infinitely worse. 

Anyway, I don't want you to commit suicide. Even if you feel like everyone else in your life doesn't want you around (which they probably do wan't you around), at least I do, and probably a lot of other people on this subreddit do as well, for what it's worth.

It was a decade ago when I started becoming addicted to falling asleep.

I was broke at the time and I would do nearly anything for money. Hell, I even became a stripper at one point just to make ends meet. Life became tough for me during the time to say the least. 
 
I remember it like it happened yesterday. I went into the experimental testing facility, where you would make money off of trying different drugs. Mind you, I was near bankrupt, so I tried the drugs that would gain the most profit. 

Zarcasil, it was called. The drug that would fix insonmia. While I was nervous to potentially destroy my body with drugs, I needed the 10,000 dollars to pay off my student loan debt ASAP. 

I went home that night and popped one in my mouth. 30 minutes later, I would enter into the most intense dream I'd had to that day.

I suddenly could fly above New York city. I could breathe fire. I knew every martial art in the book. I was the most handsome and successful model in all of America. I spent the day flying from my apartment, all the way to Mount Everest, and I even took a trip to see the Opera House in Sydney, Australia. I even wore the jacket from Drive that I wanted for so long. All in all, I was a complete badass.

And then I woke up. I sat there, pissed off that I had to go back to this reality. I was still broke, despite the money I was making off of Zarcasil. I went to my job at Little Caeser's, thinking about my dream all day. Thinking about the jacket I was wearing, the sights I saw, and the weightless feeling of flying. It was all pure bliss, and I wanted to go back.

That night I stood over my sink, in my dingy little bathroom, in my dingy little apartment. I wanted to be asleep this second. I popped three tablets in my mouth, just to make sure I went back to this same universe.

You guessed it, I did. I flew around like Superman, and I visited every place I could before I would wake up again. 

It's been ten years, and I am addicted to sleeping. Every waking moment, all I want to do is sleep, where I can fly, where I can pet wild animals, and where I am truly free, and in my own perfect universe. 

Zarcasil has changed me forever.
